result_text:
Dataclasses defined inside a function now work. Your example, plus a `List[Foo]` field, round-trips through `from_dict` and `to_dict`. A missing field raises `MissingField` instead of a syntax error.

I didn't use the `CodeBuilder` wrapper from the issue. `type_name` now handles it, in `mashumaro/core/meta/helpers.py`. For a non-short name whose `__qualname__` contains `<locals>`, it returns a flat identifier, such as `__main___f__locals__Foo`. A new helper, `local_type_alias`, builds that identifier. `add_type_modules` in `mashumaro/core/meta/code/builder.py` registers each such type in the generated code's globals under that name. Short names, used in error messages, are unchanged.

I ran the full suite, stopping at the first failure. 26151 passed and 1 failed: `tests/test_pep_646.py::test_type_name_for_unpacks_py_less_than_311`. That test fails the same way with my change stashed. The run stopped there, so any tests after it didn't run.

I didn't add a test for the local-class case, per your instructions.
